messages:
Alex: Heads-up — we're about to roll the new audit-export flow to canary tenants. Quick ops question: how do we want quota gating to behave for large downloads? e.g., 50GB /tenant exports.
Maria: +1 on canary. My thought: console should show estimated size + a 'preview (sample)' toggle so users can get a 1k-event sample before queuing full export. saves quota surprises.
Jen: Agree on preview. Implementation Q: should preview be a cheap NDJSON sample from the changefeed or rely on the same export job but with sampling params? sampling at source is cheaper.
Sam: From infra POV we need to protect the export pipeline. We should enforce both per-tenant concurrent export cap and a monthly download credit. otherwise noisy tenants can OOM the worker pool.
Alex: Ok. UX asks: show two progress states in console: "Queued (preview)" and "Queued (full)" with separate ETA estimates. Also show estimated cost in tokens/credits.
Maria: For pre-signed downloads, we should TTL-limit and revoke on entitlement change. e.g., presigned_url ttl=24h and revoke if tenant entitlement removed.
Jen: API debate: one endpoint vs two endpoints. Option A: POST /exports with {mode: sample|full} Option B: POST /exports/samples then POST /exports. Two endpoints simplifies RBAC/scopes. Thoughts?
Alex: I'm leaning two endpoints to keep sampling light-weight and avoid accidental full exports via automation.
Sam: Two endpoints also simplifies quota checks. sample uses a cheap quota bucket (preview_credits) separate from full_export_credits.
Maria: Console wiring: when sample is requested, show a small inline preview (first 50 events). If they accept, offer a single-click promote to full export that reuses the same manifest id.
Jen: Implementation note: manifest id can be immutable. sample job writes manifest: {id, sample=true, sample_size}. full job can reference manifest.id and request expansion. Saves double scanning. Example API: 
``` 
POST /api/v1/exports
{ "manifest_id": "m-123", "mode":"promote" }
```
Alex: Nice. Any concerns about telemetry? We need per-route traces to track scan time vs packaging time vs presign latency.
Sam: Add a metric: export_bytes_scanned, export_bytes_sent, export_manifest_prep_time. Hook these into console timeline.
Maria: Also add a signal for "preview_accepted" so product can measure conversion from preview->full.
Jen: Edge case: if tenant has <full_export_credit but sample accepted, should we surface a soft-fail CTA and allow an invoice / approval flow?
Alex: Product decision but console should show a clear blocker: "Insufficient export credits — request escalation" with contact link.
Sam: We'll need enforcement in the API gateway: return 402 with structured error that includes resolution_url. Example response: 
``` 
HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required
{
  "error": "insufficient_export_credits",
  "required": "125GB",
  "resolve_url": "https://console.redwood.ai/tenant/abc/export-credits"
}
```
export-bot: Export job m-123: sample completed; 50 events written; size=12KB; duration=1.2s.
Maria: Sample looks good. Moving to canary promote button in console.
Jen: I'll open a PR for the two-endpoint approach + manifest reuse pattern. Will add telemetry spans and quota checks.
Alex: Thanks — let's track rollout with a small canary (5 tenants) and telemetry alerts for export_manifest_prep_time > 30s.
Sam: I'll add the quota guard in the gateway and the 402 payload.
Maria: UX will add preview->promote CTA and estimated cost badge.
Alex: Perfect. If anyone wants to pair on the manifest schema, ping me. :thumbsup:
